80: 
81:                 // Keep the prompt inside the model's context: old tool output is
82:                 // excerpted and, if needed, old rounds are dropped.
83:                 val request = HistoryTrimmer.trim(full, maxHistoryChars)
84:                 if (request !== full && !trimmed) {
85:                     trimmed = true
86:                     onEvent(Event.Note("История хода сокращена, чтобы запрос уложился в контекст модели"))
87:                 }
88: 
89:                 val preview = StringBuilder()
90:                 var lastEmit = 0L
91:                 val response = try {
92:                     clientFactory().chat(request, tools.definitions(), isCancelled) { delta ->
93:                         preview.append(delta)
94:                         val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
95:                         if (now - lastEmit > 400) {
96:                             lastEmit = now
97:                             onEvent(Event.Thinking(preview.toString()))
98:                         }
99:                     }
100:                 } finally {
101:                     onEvent(Event.Thinking(""))
102:                 }
103: 
104:                 if (response.toolCalls.isEmpty() && response.content.isNullOrBlank()) {
105:                     // Nothing usable came back. Nudge once instead of ending the
106:                     // turn in silence; the budget still counts this round.
107:                     full.put(JSONObject().put("role", "assistant").put("content", "(пустой ответ)"))
108:                     full.put(JSONObject().put("role", "user").put("content", CONTINUE_NUDGE))
109:                     continue
110:                 }
111: 
112:                 if (response.toolCalls.isEmpty()) {
113:                     val text = response.content.orEmpty()
114:                     full.put(JSONObject().put("role", "assistant").put("content", text))
115:                     if (text.isNotBlank()) onEvent(Event.AssistantText(text))
116:                     return finish(full)
117:                 }
118: 
119:                 val assistantMsg = JSONObject().put("role", "assistant")
120:                 if (response.content != null) {
121:                     assistantMsg.put("content", response.content)
122:                     if (response.content.isNotBlank()) onEvent(Event.AssistantText(response.content))
123:                 }
124:                 val calls = JSONArray()
125:                 response.toolCalls.forEach { call ->
126:                     calls.put(
127:                         JSONObject().apply {
128:                             put("id", call.id)
129:                             put("type", "function")
130:                             put("function", JSONObject().put("name", call.name).put("arguments", call.arguments))
131:                         },
132:                     )
133:                 }
134:                 assistantMsg.put("tool_calls", calls)
135:                 full.put(assistantMsg)
136: 
137:                 var interrupted = false
138:                 for (call in response.toolCalls) {
139:                     if (isCancelled()) {
140:                         interrupted = true
141:                         break
142:                     }
143:                     onEvent(Event.ToolStart(call.name, prettyArgs(call.arguments)))
144:                     val result = tools.execute(call.name, call.arguments)
145:                     onEvent(Event.ToolDone(call.name, result))
146:                     full.put(
147:                         JSONObject().apply {
148:                             put("role", "tool")
149:                             put("tool_call_id", call.id)
150:                             put("content", result)
151:                         },
152:                     )
153:                 }
154:                 if (interrupted) {
155:                     // The calls that never ran are answered by finish(), which
156:                     // repairs the tail of the history before it is saved.
157:                     onEvent(Event.Failed(CANCELLED))
158:                     break
159:                 }
160:             }
161:             if (!isCancelled() && budget <= 0) {
162:                 onEvent(
163:                     Event.Failed(
164:                         "достигнут лимит раундов ($maxSteps) — файлы и история сохранены, " +
165:                             "напишите /continue, и агент продолжит с этого места",
166:                     ),
167:                 )
168:             }
169:         } catch (t: Throwable) {
170:             onEvent(Event.Failed(t.message ?: t.javaClass.simpleName))
171:         }
172:         return finish(full)
173:     }
174: 
175:     /**
176:      * Ends the turn: answers any tool call that never got a result (a stopped
177:      * or failed round) and drops the system message. A history with an
178:      * unanswered tool call is rejected by strict providers, and this history is
179:      * what the next request and the next session are built from.
180:      */
181:     private fun finish(messages: JSONArray): JSONArray {
182:         val answered = mutableSetOf<String>()
183:         for (i in 0 until messages.length()) {
184:             val m = messages.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
185:             if (m.optString("role") == "tool") answered += m.optString("tool_call_id")
186:         }
187:         for (i in messages.length() - 1 downTo 0) {
188:             val m = messages.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
189:             if (m.optString("role") != "assistant") continue
190:             val calls = m.optJSONArray("tool_calls") ?: return stripSystem(messages)
191:             for (c in 0 until calls.length()) {
192:                 val id = calls.getJSONObject(c).optString("id")
193:                 if (id.isEmpty() || id in answered) continue
194:                 messages.put(
195:                     JSONObject()
196:                         .put("role", "tool")
197:                         .put("tool_call_id", id)
198:                         .put("content", "(выполнение прервано — ход остановлен)"),
199:                 )
200:             }
201:             break
202:         }
203:         return stripSystem(messages)
204:     }
205: 
206:     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- prompt
207: 
208:     private fun systemMessage(): JSONObject {
209:         // instructions (AGENTS.md etc.) for the current project
210:         val instr = Instructions(workspace).collect(projectDir)
211:         val todosBlock = if (tools.todos.isEmpty()) {
212:             "No todos yet."
213:         } else {
214:             tools.todos.joinToString("\n") { "  - [${it.status}] ${it.content}" }
215:         }
216: 
217:         val prompt = buildString {
218:             appendLine("You are opencode, an AI coding agent running inside the PocketRun app on Android. You help with code and files in the user's sandbox.")
219:             appendLine()
220:             appendLine("# Environment")
221:             appendLine("- Project directory: ${projectDir?.relativeToOrNull(workspace.root)?.path ?: "."} (relative paths in tools resolve there)")
222:             appendLine("- Sandbox root: the workspace; nothing outside it is accessible.")
223:             appendLine("- The `bash` tool is a restricted mini-shell: ${MiniShell.COMMANDS.joinToString(", ")}.")
224:             appendLine("  - `python` runs CPython 3.13 (standard library only, no pip);")
225:             appendLine("  - `node` runs a Node.js-compatible layer (require/fs/timers/Buffer/http work; no class/async-await/import syntax);")
226:             appendLine("  - `npx <pkg> [args]` installs and runs pure-JS npm packages (no native addons; prefer older releases of big packages, e.g. cowsay@1.4.0);")
227:             appendLine("  - `npm init -y`, `npm install <pkg>`, `npm run <script>`, `npm ls` manage a real node project: package.json is created in the project, installed packages are visible to require(), scripts run through the shell. Pure-JS packages only (no native addons).")
228:             appendLine("  - commands may run up to ${OpenCodeTools.BASH_TIMEOUT_MS / 60_000} minutes each; `sleep` up to ${MiniShell.MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS} seconds.")
229:             appendLine("- `webfetch` can read documentation pages.")
230:             appendLine()
231:             appendLine("# How to work")
232:             appendLine("- Explore first (list, read, glob, grep), then act (edit, write, apply_patch, bash), then verify by running code.")
233:             appendLine("- Prefer precise edits over rewriting whole files.")
234:             appendLine("- Use todowrite for multi-step tasks; keep the list current.")
235:             appendLine("- Ask the user with the question tool when requirements are ambiguous.")
236:             appendLine("- If a tool fails, read the error and adjust; do not repeat the same failing call more than twice.")
237:             appendLine("- Keep going until the task is actually done: you have up to $maxSteps model rounds for this request, and long builds and downloads are normal — plan for them instead of stopping early.")
238:             appendLine("- When you must wait for something (a CI run, a build), block on a single waiting call (github run_wait) instead of polling in a loop: polling wastes rounds.")
239:             appendLine("- For workflows the user repeats, suggest saving a skill: a folder .opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with `name` and `description` in YAML frontmatter — you can create it with apply_patch yourself, then load it with the skill tool.")
240:             appendLine("- Answer in the user's language (usually Russian). Be concise; show what you did.")
241:             if (askMode) {
242:                 appendLine()
243:                 appendLine("# Clarification mode (user preference)")
244:                 appendLine("Before any non-trivial task, ask the user 1-3 short clarifying questions with the question tool (each with concrete answer options). Only proceed automatically when the request is completely unambiguous or you already asked in this session.")
245:             }
246:             if (hasGitHub) {
247:                 appendLine()
248:                 appendLine("# GitHub and Actions runners")
249:                 appendLine("The `github` tool talks to the GitHub REST API with the user's token. GitHub Actions runners are full Linux machines (ubuntu-latest): use them for anything the mobile sandbox cannot run — npm packages, opencode itself, compilers, heavy tests.")
250:                 appendLine("Runner pattern:")
251:                 appendLine("1. repo_create (private by default) → 2. push code + .github/workflows/run.yml (one commit, atomically) → 3. dispatch → 4. github run_wait {repo, timeout_sec} — blocks until the run finishes and returns the conclusion, the jobs and the log tail → 5. artifacts/artifact_download.")
252:                 appendLine("Never poll `runs` in a loop: run_wait is one round instead of ten, and it works for anything that takes minutes.")
253:                 appendLine("Example workflow the user can adapt:")
254:                 appendLine("```yaml")
255:                 appendLine("name: agent-runner")
256:                 appendLine("on: workflow_dispatch")
257:                 appendLine("jobs:")
258:                 appendLine("  run:")
259:                 appendLine("    runs-on: ubuntu-latest")
260:                 appendLine("    steps:")
261:                 appendLine("      - uses: actions/checkout@v4")
262:                 appendLine("      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4")
263:                 appendLine("        with: { node-version: 22 }")
264:                 appendLine("      - run: npm install")
265:                 appendLine("      # opencode inside the runner:")
266:                 appendLine("      - run: npm i -g opencode-ai && opencode run --model opencode/claude-sonnet-4-5 \"<task>\"")
267:                 appendLine("        env: { OPENCODE_API_KEY: '${'$'}{{ secrets.ZEN_KEY }}' }")
268:                 appendLine("      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4")
269:                 appendLine("        with: { name: out, path: out/ }")
270:                 appendLine("```")
271:                 appendLine("Never print or commit the user's tokens; reference secrets like \${{ secrets.NAME }} instead.")
272:             }
273:             appendLine()
274:             appendLine("# Current todos")
275:             appendLine(todosBlock)
276:             if (instr.text.isNotEmpty()) {
277:                 appendLine()
278:                 appendLine("# Instructions")
279:                 appendLine(instr.text)
280:             }
281:         }
282:         return JSONObject().put("role", "system").put("content", prompt.trim())
283:     }
284: 
285:     private fun stripSystem(messages: JSONArray): JSONArray {
286:         val out = JSONArray()
287:         for (i in 0 until messages.length()) {
288:             val m = messages.get(i)
289:             if (m is JSONObject && m.optString("role") == "system") continue
290:             out.put(m)
291:         }
292:         return out
293:     }
294: 
295:     private fun prettyArgs(argsJson: String): String = try {
296:         val obj = JSONObject(argsJson)
297:         if (obj.length() == 0) "" else obj.toString().take(200)
298:     } catch (t: Throwable) {
299:         argsJson.take(200)
300:     }
301: }

(End of file - total 301 lines)
</content>

import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

/**
 * The opencode agent loop: user message in, tool calls out, tool results back
 * in, repeat until a plain-text answer (or the round budget). The system prompt
 * is assembled opencode-style: base agent prompt + AGENTS.md instructions +
 * current todos; skills are advertised through the `skill` tool description.

 * them: the answer is streamed (so the connection never goes idle and ⏹ works),
 * the history is trimmed before every request (so the prompt stays inside the
 * model's context), and a turn that runs out of rounds is saved instead of lost
 * — the user continues it with `/continue`.
 */

display.text:
package dev.pocketrun.agent

import android.content.Context

/**
 * Agent configuration, stored in SharedPreferences. Works with any
 * OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq,
 * Together, a local llama.cpp/vLLM server on the Wi-Fi network, …
 *
 * Also carries the agent-behaviour knobs (permission mode, max rounds) and
 * the optional GitHub token used by the `github` tool.
 */
object AgentSettings {

    const val DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
    const val DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-4o-mini"

    /** opencode Zen: the curated OpenAI-compatible gateway from opencode.ai/auth. */
    const val ZEN_BASE_URL = "https://opencode.ai/zen/v1"
    const val ZEN_AUTH_URL = "https://opencode.ai/auth"

    /** Where the user creates a GitHub PAT (scopes: repo, workflow). */
    const val GITHUB_TOKEN_URL = "https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo,workflow&description=PocketRun"
    const val GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com"

    /** Permission modes for tool execution. */
    const val MODE_AUTO = "auto"     // everything runs without asking
    const val MODE_MANUAL = "manual" // mutations need a tap; reads run freely
    const val MODE_ASK = "ask"       // the agent asks clarifying questions first
    val MODES = listOf(MODE_AUTO, MODE_MANUAL, MODE_ASK)
    val MODE_LABELS = mapOf(MODE_AUTO to "Авто", MODE_MANUAL to "Вручную", MODE_ASK to "Вопросы")

    /**
     * Model rounds per user request. Each round is one model call plus the
     * tools it asked for, so a real task (edit a project, push it, wait for the
     * CI run, fix what broke) needs dozens of them — the old default of 12
     * stopped agents in the middle of ordinary work.
     */
    const val DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS = 40
    const val MAX_STEPS_LIMIT = 500

    /** Ready-made presets shown in the model settings dialog. */
    data class Preset(val label: String, val baseUrl: String, val model: String)

    val PRESETS = listOf(
        Preset("OpenCode Zen", ZEN_BASE_URL, "claude-sonnet-4-5"),
        Preset("OpenAI", "https://api.openai.com/v1", "gpt-4o-mini"),
        Preset("OpenRouter", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"),
        Preset("Groq", "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"),
    )

    data class Config(
        val baseUrl: String = DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
        val apiKey: String = "",
        val model: String = DEFAULT_MODEL,
        val githubToken: String = "",
        val confirmMode: String = MODE_AUTO,
        val maxSteps: Int = DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS,
    ) {
        /**
         * The API key is optional: local servers (llama.cpp, vLLM) need none,
         * and for Zen the server itself answers 403 without one — which the
         * agent surfaces with a hint. Only URL and model are required.
         */
        val isReady: Boolean get() = baseUrl.isNotBlank() && model.isNotBlank()
        val endpoint: String get() = baseUrl.trimEnd('/') + "/chat/completions"
        val isZen: Boolean get() = baseUrl.contains("opencode.ai/zen")
        val hasGitHub: Boolean get() = githubToken.isNotBlank()
        val safeMaxSteps: Int get() = maxSteps.coerceIn(1, MAX_STEPS_LIMIT)
    }

    private const val PREFS = "agent"

    fun read(context: Context): Config {
        val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        return Config(
            baseUrl = prefs.getString("baseUrl", DEFAULT_BASE_URL)!!.trim().trimEnd('/').ifBlank { DEFAULT_BASE_URL },
            apiKey = prefs.getString("apiKey", "")!!.trim(),
            model = prefs.getString("model", DEFAULT_MODEL)!!.trim().ifBlank { DEFAULT_MODEL },
            githubToken = prefs.getString("githubToken", "")!!.trim(),
            confirmMode = prefs.getString("confirmMode", MODE_AUTO)!!.trim().let { if (it in MODES) it else MODE_AUTO },
            maxSteps = prefs.getString("maxSteps", DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS.toString())!!.trim().toIntOrNull() ?: DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS,
        )
    }

    fun save(context: Context, config: Config) {
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            .edit()
            .putString("baseUrl", config.baseUrl.trim().trimEnd('/'))
            .putString("apiKey", config.apiKey.trim())
            .putString("model", config.model.trim())
            .putString("githubToken", config.githubToken.trim())
            .putString("confirmMode", config.confirmMode)
            .putString("maxSteps", config.safeMaxSteps.toString())
            .apply()
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- ui state

    /**
     * Which session tab was active and which tabs were open, so the agent
     * chat comes back exactly as it was after the app is closed. Returns null
     * when nothing was saved yet (first launch → continue the latest session).
     */
    data class UiState(val lastSessionId: String?, val openTabs: List<String>)

    fun readUiState(context: Context): UiState? {
        val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        if (!prefs.contains("uiOpenTabs")) return null
        val last = prefs.getString("uiLastSessionId", "")!!.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
        val tabs = prefs.getString("uiOpenTabs", "")!!.split(',').filter { it.isNotBlank() }
        return UiState(last, tabs)
    }

    fun saveUiState(context: Context, lastSessionId: String?, openTabs: List<String>) {
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            .edit()
            .putString("uiLastSessionId", lastSessionId ?: "")

40:         val blocks = blocks(messages)
41:         // A history with an orphan `tool` message has to be rebuilt even when it
42:         // is small: the API rejects it whole, and the next round is the answer.
43:         val repaired = blocks.sumOf { it.messages.size } < messages.length() - 1

54:         // request that carries the original task.
55:         val kept = ArrayList(shrunk)

23:  * * **Retries.** Timeouts, resets, 429 and 5xx are retried with a backoff;
24:  *   everything else (bad key, unknown model) fails immediately.

I have enough now. Let me do a final check on a couple of specific things: MiniShell `runCodeFile` uses `workspace.cache/opencode-shell/cmd.py` and passes `cwd=dir` — fine. Also check `MiniShell.executeSync` for python/node - they ignore `request.stdin` (stdin is null) — that's the pipe-stdin issue already noted.

Let me also verify the `python -c` / `node -e` scratch file: it writes to `workspace.cache/opencode-shell/cmd.py`, and passes cwd = dir. Python adds script_dir to sys.path — so the cache dir is on sys.path. Minor.

One more important check: NpxRuntime `resolveBin` at line 365 — `File(pkgDir, rel).toPath().normalize().toFile()` — no sandbox containment check (no Workspace.resolve). A malicious/broken package.json bin of `../../../../etc/x` could point outside. But packages are inside workspace so path traversal could reach anywhere in workspace root... but also could go outside workspace? `packages/<name>` — `../../..` from there → workspace root's parent, i.e. filesDir. That's a real finding: no containment check on bin path.

Also TarReader.extract → safeFile checks. Good.

Also `NpxRuntime.install` line 213-215: if existing version doesn't satisfy, it deletes and reinstalls. Fine.

`installInto` at line 273: `val target = if (topVer != null) nested else top` — the "hoist" logic.

Let me also double check one thing: MiniShell `pwd` line 173 — confirmed the bug: `dir.relativeToOrNull(...)?.let { "./$it" } ?: dir.absolutePath + "\n"` — when relative succeeds, no "\n". Confirmed real.

`wc` line 341: `files.last()` — confirmed only last file.

`head/tail` line 330: `files[0]` — confirmed.

`grep` line 386-389: `rest[1]` only — confirmed; and flags other than -i/-n are dropped from rest (filtered out) so they're silently ignored — confirmed line 379.

Glob: `globToRegex` at OpenCodeTools 546-561 and MiniShell 596-611: `**` → `.*` so `**/*.py` → `.*/[^/]*\.py` which requires a `/`. Confirmed both.

GitHubClient line 31 READ_OPS: missing artifact_download. Confirmed.

GitHubClient line 172: `changes.forEach { contentsDelete(...) }` result discarded → reports "удалено" regardless. Confirmed.

GitHubClient line 253 `?: "?"`. Confirmed.

seconds() 363-369 catch → 0. Confirmed.

Workspace normalize: `toPath().normalize()` is lexical, not canonical → symlink escape possible. Confirmed as lexical-only. Note: TarReader skips symlinks so no symlink creation via npm; but Python's `os.symlink` exists in the sandbox? Python isn't jailed at all — see below.

pocketrun.py: no jail. `run()` runs runpy with full os access. So Workspace.kt's claim "nothing outside the sandbox is exposed" is false for Python. This is CORE.

Let me verify one more time that Python has no restriction: `sys.path.insert(0, script_dir)`, `os.chdir(cwd)` — cwd comes from `request.cwd` which is set by MiniShell as `dir` (sandboxed) or by AppViewModel. No chroot, no path filter. Confirmed CORE.

Also NpxRuntime line 365 resolveBin — no workspace containment.

Also `OpenCodeTools.doGlob`/`doGrep` line 364/381 fallback to workspace.root when the path isn't a directory. Confirmed.

`doQuestion` 468. Confirmed.

Api schema: description says `api{method,path,body?}` (line 229) but schema declares `api_path` (line 251) and impl uses `args.getString("api_path")` (line 523). Model following description sends `path` → JSONException → "error: No value for api_path". Confirmed MINOR/IMPORTANT.

JsRuntime 216 `catch (_: Exception) { }` around `__prOnExit` — swallows user cleanup errors. MINOR.
JsRuntime 221 flush in finally — MINOR.
MiniShell 565 writeToFile catch empty → redirect failure silent, returns exit code 0. Confirmed: line 152-155 `writeToFile(redirectFile, input, append); return Result(r.exitCode, "")`. So `echo x > /nonexistent/../..`? Well sandboxPath resolves so it's inside. But write failure (e.g., path is a directory) → silent success. Confirmed IMPORTANT-ish MINOR.

Also MiniShell 200 env constant, 208 uname constant. 249 ls directory size 0 (line 235 `e.length()` for dirs). MINOR.

MiniShell 142-145: pipes into python/node/npx ignore stdin (documented at 140). But note the comment claims "runtime commands ignore stdin/pipes" — and the pipeline loop sets `input = r.output` then passes `input` only to builtins. So `echo x | python script.py` gives empty stdin. IMPORTANT.

Also there's a subtle bug: for non-final stages, `input` is set to r.output — fine.

Also `runCodeFile(ext, ...)` at line 546 — the `ext` parameter is never used! Let me verify: `private fun runCodeFile(ext: String, code: String, dir: File, timeoutMs: Long, python: Boolean)` and body uses `if (python) "py" else "js"` — `ext` unused. Confirmed unused parameter (user asked for "parameters accepted but never used"). Callers pass "py"/"js" at 404 and 421.

Sessions.load 80-82: catch → null (silent). Confirmed. Also `list()` 59 runCatching → null.

Instructions 83-85: opencode.json parse failure → emptyList (silent). 110-112: remote fetch failure → null (silent, documented-ish). 96-98: glob entries only use the FIRST .md file — the comment itself says "For now single-file entries cover the common case; glob entries use the first match." That's a real degradation with a self-admitted TODO-ish comment. IMPORTANT.

ApplyPatch: no obvious bug. `*** Delete File` skipped if not found (line 121) — reported as "skipped", visible. OK.

OpenCodeAgent 26: `maxSteps: Int = 12` default, but AppViewModel always passes config.safeMaxSteps. Test? Let me note as MINOR (stale default vs AgentSettings.DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS=40).

Now: unused things:
- `Exec.kt` `ScriptRuntime` interface — grep found no implementations ("ScriptRuntime" search returned nothing outside Exec.kt? Actually the grep excluded Exec.kt and found nothing). So `ScriptRuntime`, `RuntimeKind.from`, `ExecResult.isSuccess` are unused dead code. Confirmed by the grep: "== ScriptRuntime" (nothing), "== RuntimeKind.from" (nothing), "== isSuccess" (nothing).
- `AgentSettings.GITHUB_API` and `ZEN_AUTH_URL` — declared but GITHUB_API grep showed only the definition. Let me check ZEN_AUTH_URL — only definition at line 20. Both unused (AppViewModel may hardcode). Let me verify quickly.

Also `Workspace.logs` — grep for `.logs` found only the github op; so `Workspace.logs` (line 16) appears unused.

Let me do one last verification grep for these dead symbols, then write the report.

Also check `Sessions` `delete`/`export` used from UI? Probably yes.

I have gathered a thorough picture. Let me do a few final checks on some specifics I want to confirm before writing the report:

1. `resolveBin` — no sandbox check on the resolved bin path (normalize but no root containment) — a package's `bin` field could point outside (`../../..`). Since packages are extracted with TarReader safeFile, but `bin` in package.json is arbitrary. `File(pkgDir, rel).toPath().normalize().toFile()` — no containment check. Then js.execute with target = binPath.absolutePath, and JsRuntime.readMainSource reads `File(request.target)` directly — no sandbox check! So a malicious npm package with `"bin": "../../../../etc/passwd"` could run arbitrary files outside sandbox. Actually JsRuntime.execute -> runLocked -> readMainSource(state.request) which does `File(request.target).readText()` without workspace.resolve. That's a real sandbox bypass. Good CORE finding.

Also `readMainSource` doesn't check the file is inside the workspace — any absolute path works. Who calls JsRuntime.execute? AppViewModel.runScript (resolves via sandbox probably), NpxRuntime (bin path). Let me verify AppViewModel runScript.

2. MiniShell runCodeFile: writes scratch file into workspace.cache — fine. But python/node `-c` executed with `cwd = dir` and the file at cache path. Fine.

3. `MiniShell` `runPython`/`runNode` don't pass stdin — `ExecRequest(...)` has no stdin field set → null. So `echo x | cat` works for builtins, but `python script.py` reading sys.stdin gets nothing. That's the pipe limitation already noted.

4. `runCodeFile(ext, ...)` — `ext` parameter unused. MINOR.

5. `NpxRuntime.install` — no integrity (`dist.integrity`/`shasum`) verification. CORE-ish security finding. Confirmed: no `integrity` reference in NpxRegistry/NpxRuntime.

6. `TarReader`: for 'x'/'g' pax headers, size read and data consumed — fine, but pax headers can contain a `path` override for long names; the entry after pax uses truncated name. Also `'L'` (GNU long name) — the long name data is consumed but NOT applied, so the file gets the truncated 100-char name. Real break. Also note: for type '2' symlinks skipped → packages that need symlinks break. Also entries with size > Int.MAX would break; minor.

Also a bug: for directory entries type '5', it reads `data` (size) anyway — fine.

Another TarReader bug: `readFully(gz, header)` then `if (name.isEmpty()) skipData(gz, size)` — but then it continues to `val data = if (size > 0) readExact(gz, size)` — double-skip! Wait: line 32: `if (name.isEmpty()) skipData(gz, size)`, then line 34 reads the data anyway. If name is empty, it skips the data and then tries to read `size` more bytes → corrupt stream. But name empty is rare. Actually that's a real bug but rare trigger. Worth listing as MINOR.

7. `Semver.satisfiesString` with `existing != null && spec.version?.let { Semver.isSupportedRange(it) } != false` in NpxRuntime.install line 213: if spec.version is a range that doesn't match existing, it reinstalls. OK.

8. `Workspace.resolve` — uses `toPath().normalize()` which is lexical, not canonical → symlink escape. But can a user create a symlink? Python `os.symlink` is available in CPython stdlib! Python runs in-process with full access. So Python can create a symlink in the workspace pointing outside and then read arbitrary app files (license key in SharedPreferences, keystore? no). Actually more importantly, Python has FULL filesystem access — `open('/data/data/dev.pocketrun/...')` works. The Workspace claim "nothing outside the sandbox is exposed" is FALSE for Python. This is the CORE finding. pocketrun.py does not chroot or restrict. Python `os` module fully functional. PLAN.md line 8-9 of Workspace.kt claims user code can reach them through "the Python `os` module" but nothing outside is exposed — that's false.

Let me verify: PythonRuntime.execute passes request.target (absolute path) and cwd. No restriction. pocketrun.py `run()` uses runpy.run_path. No chroot. Chaquopy runs in-process with app's UID. So Python code can read `/data/user/0/dev.pocketrun/shared_prefs/license.xml` (the stored license key) and any app file. This is a genuine CORE sandbox finding. The system prompt also says "Sandbox root: the workspace; nothing outside it is accessible" — a false claim to the model.

9. `NpmRegistry` — no integrity check, allows any http(s) tarball URL (dist.tarball from metadata, could point anywhere). Also `metadata()` full doc download unbounded (comment says can be MBs). Fine.

10. `OpenCodeTools.doGlob`/`doGrep` walk the whole workspace from root when path isn't a dir — silent fallback, confirmed at 364/381.

11. Glob `**/*.py` — `globToRegex` maps `**` → `.*` and then `/` literal → `^.*/[^/]*\.py$` requires a slash → top-level `foo.py` NOT matched. Confirmed CORE for the documented example. Same bug in MiniShell.globMatch line 596 and used by `find -name` (which also tries f.name so find is ok).

12. GitHubClient READ_OPS missing `artifact_download` — read-only op classified as mutating → manual mode asks approval for a read. MINOR/IMPORTANT (UX). Also `api` with GET is classified as mutating (test asserts isReadOnly false for api) — fine, conservative.

13. `commit()` delete fallback line 171-174: contentsDelete result ignored; returns success message. Confirmed real.

14. `seconds()` catch returns 0 → duration shows "0с" for failed runs. MINOR.

15. `contentsCommit` line 253 `?: "?"` — cosmetic.

16. `doWrite` — writes without limit; fine.

17. `doRead` — `f.readText` on huge file then truncates to 32K; reads whole file into memory. MINOR.

18. `doSkill` returns `skill.content.take(32*1024)` — silent truncation without marker. MINOR.

19. `Instructions.resolveInstructionPath` — glob entries only return the FIRST .md file; comment at 96-97 admits "For now single-file entries cover the common case; glob entries use the first match." That's a documented partial implementation → real finding (IMPORTANT). Also silently: only first file included.

20. `Instructions.fetchRemote` catch → null silently (line 110-112). Important-ish: remote instructions silently omitted from prompt. MINOR/IMPORTANT.

21. `Sessions.load` catch → null (line 80-82) — corrupt session silently disappears. Test `corruptedFileIgnored` codifies it. MINOR.

22. `OpenCodeAgent` maxSteps default 12 in constructor but AppViewModel always passes config.safeMaxSteps (40). Not a real bug in production path. But the KDoc line 237 says "you have up to $maxSteps model rounds". Fine. Not a finding — the default is only used if constructed directly. Downgrade/remove.

23. `Exec.OutputListener` default no-op methods — not a real finding (interface with defaults, all impls override what's needed). Remove from report or MINOR.

24. `Workspace.logs` — unused property. Dead code, MINOR/trivial. Probably not worth reporting. Skip or minor.

25. `AgentSettings.GITHUB_API` and `ZEN_AUTH_URL` — unused constants (UI hardcodes the URL strings). MINOR dead code. And AgentScreen hardcodes "https://opencode.ai/auth" instead of using ZEN_AUTH_URL. MINOR.

26. `pocketrun.py` PipeStream.close catch pass (line 57-61) — benign cleanup. Trivial; probably skip or MINOR.

27. `JsRuntime` line 216 `catch (_: Exception) { }` around `__prOnExit` — swallows errors from user 'exit' handlers. MINOR. Line 221 flush catch — benign.

28. UI: `AgentScreen.kt:653` and `:725` `onClick = {}` — these are combinedClickable where the tap does nothing (only long-press copies). Deliberate but a no-op tap handler. MINOR (matches user's "UI do nothing" criterion, but it's a design choice). Worth a MINOR mention.

29. `ActivationScreen.kt:71` `else -> {}` — the `Active` state never reaches this screen (App.kt routes Active → MainScreen), so it's exhaustive-when filler. Not a finding.

30. `EditorScreen.kt:102` `RunState.Idle -> {}` — legitimate no-op branch for "no status text". Not a finding.

31. `MiniShell` `env` (line 200) and `uname` (line 208) return hardcoded constants — deliberate documented. MINOR.

32. `ls -l` shows 0 bytes for directories (line 235) — real minor bug.

33. `wc` only last file (line 341), `head`/`tail` only first file (line 330), `grep` only rest[1] (line 386-388) and drops all flags except -i (line 379) — real correctness bugs in an agent-facing shell. IMPORTANT each (agent uses `grep -r`? -r unsupported → returns matches from stdin = empty). Actually `grep -r pattern .` → rest = ["pattern", "."] (both non-dash) → treats "." as the file → readText on a directory → `sandboxPath(".")?.takeIf{isFile}` → null → "нет такого файла". So `grep -r` fails with a confusing message. Real.

34. `pwd` newline bug line 173 — real MINOR. Verified: `dir.relativeToOrNull(...)?.let {"./$it"} ?: dir.absolutePath + "\n"` — when inside root, no trailing newline; when outside (can't happen), has one. Yes bug.

35. Pipeline: `input = r.output` for each stage, but the first stage gets `input` = "" always; and redirects only apply to the last stage (line 150-156). `python -c 'print(1)' > file` — python is stage 0 of 1 stage, so index == lastIndex → redirect applies. Good. But `echo hi | cat > f` works. `cat < file` unsupported (no `<` parsing) → `cat` with stdin "" → returns empty. Real: no input redirection support despite `>` `>>` being supported. MINOR/IMPORTANT.

36. `MiniShell.execute` — `||` not supported (only `&&`), and `&` background not supported. Documented as "&&" only. MINOR.

37. `npmRun` doesn't support `--` args or `npm run-script`, `pre`/`post` hooks — real but MINOR, and `npm test` maps to `run test` which exits 1 by default from npmInit template (line 482) — that's the standard npm behavior actually. Fine.

38. `npmInstall` line 508: `JSONObject(File(installed, "package.json").readText())` — will throw if missing → caught by npm's try/catch (line 465) → Result(1,...). OK.

39. `AppViewModel.runScript` — let me check whether it sandboxes. Let me grep quickly. Actually I should verify the JsRuntime target-not-sandboxed claim: does AppViewModel call jsRuntime.execute with a workspace-resolved path? Let me check lines 728-800.

Let me do one more targeted read to confirm the JsRuntime sandbox bypass and AppViewModel run paths.

All paths below are relative to `/home/runner/hub-work/pocketrun/code/`.

## CORE

1. **`android/app/src/main/python/pocketrun.py:64-126` — Python runs with no filesystem jail.** `runpy.run_path` executes user code in-process with the app's UID, and nothing constrains `open`/`os`/`glob`. `ui/AppViewModel.kt:793-801` passes an absolute target and cwd with no containment check, and `core/Workspace.kt:6-9` claims "nothing outside the sandbox is exposed". User Python can read/write the entire app sandbox: the activated license key in SharedPreferences, every other project, the keystore-derived secrets, and `/proc/self`. The documented sandbox guarantee is false for the app's flagship runtime.

2. **`core/Workspace.kt:29-37` — `resolve()` is lexical, not canonical.** It normalizes `..` textually and never resolves symlinks, so any `Workspace.resolve` caller (all of `MiniShell`, `JsRuntime` fs/chdir/require, `OpenCodeTools.read/write/edit/glob/grep`) is escapable. Combined with #1, `os.symlink('/data/data/dev.pocketrun', ws + '/escape')` defeats the entire path gate for every other runtime.

3. **`runtime/js/JsRuntime.kt:226-231` + `runtime/npm/NpxRuntime.kt:365-366` — the JS entry point is never sandboxed.** `readMainSource` reads `File(request.target)` directly with no `Workspace.resolve`, while `resolveBin` only does `File(pkgDir, rel).toPath().normalize()` with no containment check. A package whose `package.json` declares `"bin": "../../../../../shared_prefs/..."` or `"bin": "../../../../../../etc/hosts"` gets evaluated as JavaScript. Note `JsRuntime.kt:369` *does* sandbox `require`, so the entry point is the single hole — it is the one place that must be closed.

4. **`runtime/npm/NpxRuntime.kt` / `runtime/npm/NpmRegistry.kt` — no integrity verification of any kind.** There is no reference to `integrity`, `shasum`, or `sha512` anywhere under `android/app/src/`. Registry metadata and the tarball are trusted entirely, and the tarball URL is taken from attacker-influenceable metadata. Any registry/MITM compromise becomes arbitrary JavaScript execution in the sandbox (and, via #1/#2, a full sandbox escape). This is the standard check every npm client performs.

5. **`license/LicenseManager.kt:17` — licensing has no anti-rollback.** Validity is evaluated only against `now = System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000` (`:45`, `:51`, `:81`, `:85`), and no last-seen timestamp or `elapsedRealtime` floor is persisted. Setting the device clock back before `nbf` re-activates a not-yet-valid key and past `exp` re-activates an expired key, for free, indefinitely.

6. **`agent/opencode/MiniShell.kt:596-611` — the advertised `**/*.py` pattern cannot match top-level files.** `globToRegex` turns `**` into `.*` and then keeps the following `/` literal, yielding `^.*/[^/]*\.py$`, which requires a directory separator. `OpenCodeTools.kt:141` advertises exactly this as the file-discovery pattern, so the agent's primary way to find `main.py` at a project root silently returns nothing — with exit code 0 and no warning.

## IMPORTANT

7. **`MiniShell.kt:140-146, 150-156` — piped stdin is discarded for every real runtime, and `<` is unsupported.** `input` from the previous pipeline stage is passed only to builtins; `python`/`node`/`npx` get no stdin, so `cat data.txt | python process.py` runs with empty `sys.stdin`. `>`/`>>` are supported but `<` is not, so the standard workarounds fail too. Documented in a comment, but it breaks the most common agent shell idiom.

8. **`MiniShell.kt:173` — `pwd` returns a missing trailing newline.** `dir.relativeToOrNull(...)?.let { "./$it" } ?: dir.absolutePath + "\n"` attaches the newline only in the out-of-sandbox branch, so the normal in-workspace case emits no line terminator, unlike every other command.

9. **`MiniShell.kt:337-346` — `wc` silently measures only the last file** (`files.last()`), so `wc -l a.py b.py` reports one number that looks like a total.

10. **`MiniShell.kt:330` — `head`/`tail` silently process only `files[0]`**; extra files are accepted and dropped, so `head -5 a.txt b.txt` looks successful but truncates the wrong file.

11. **`MiniShell.kt:376-394` — `grep` drops every flag except `-i` and reads only one file.** Line 379 filters out unrecognized flags without warning, and line 387 uses `rest[1]` as the only path. The most common agent call, `grep -rn pattern .`, resolves `.` as a "file", fails `takeIf { it.isFile }`, and returns `grep: .: нет такого файла` — no matches, no search.

12. **`MiniShell.kt:561-566` (used at `:153`) — redirection write failures are swallowed.** `catch (t: Throwable) { }` then `Result(r.exitCode, "")` means `python x.py > /existing-dir` reports the command's own success while nothing is written.

13. **`OpenCodeTools.kt:364, 381` — a nonexistent glob/grep path silently widens to the whole workspace.** `dir.takeIf { it.isDirectory } ?: workspace.root` means a typo'd or stale path searches every project, `packages/`, and skills instead of reporting the missing path, and returns indistinguishable results.

14. **`OpenCodeTools.kt:229` vs `:251` and `:523` — the GitHub `api` tool's schema contradicts its own description.** The description documents `api{method, path, body?}` while the schema declares `api_path` and dispatch reads `args.getString("api_path")`; a model that follows the description gets a raw `JSONException: No value for api_path` instead of a tool error.

15. **`OpenCodeTools.kt:452` — skill content is silently truncated to 32 KB** (`skill.content.take(32 * 1024)`) with no marker, so long skills lose their tail and the agent follows half the instructions.

16. **`OpenCodeTools.kt:428-445` and `agent/opencode/Instructions.kt:103-112` — agent-driven fetches have no URL restrictions.** Any `http(s)` URL including loopback, link-local, and cloud-metadata addresses is allowed, and redirects are followed, with no allow/deny list. The same gap applies to `fetchRemote` in `Instructions.kt`.

17. **`GitHubClient.kt:171-174` — the commit fallback reports false success for deletions.** `changes.forEach { contentsDelete(...) }` discards each result and then unconditionally returns a "deleted/committed" message, so a failed delete is reported to the model as applied.

18. **`GitHubClient.kt:30-32` — `artifact_download` is missing from `READ_OPS`.** It is a read-only operation, so in manual mode the app asks the user to approve a mutation and blocks the agent on a download.

19. **`runtime/npm/TarReader.kt:32-34` — an empty tar entry name desynchronizes the stream.** The code calls `skipData(gz, size)` and then still executes `readExact(gz, size)`, consuming the following entry's header/payload as data. Any nameless metadata entry corrupts everything extracted after it.

20. **`TarReader.kt:50` — PAX/GNU long names are consumed and ignored.** `else -> Unit // 'x'/'g' pax headers, ... 'L' long names: consumed, ignored` means paths longer than the ustar 100-char field are extracted under a truncated name and then fail to `require`. Scoped/long-path packages are common enough to break in practice.

21. **`MiniShell.kt:508-519` — `npm install` reads only `dependencies`.** `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `overrides`, `bundleDependencies`, and lockfiles are ignored, so installing a package that relies on them produces a silently broken dependency tree.

22. **`agent/opencode/Sessions.kt:80-82` — a corrupted session file is silently discarded** (`catch (t: Throwable) { null }`), with the behavior codified in `test/SessionsTest.kt`. The user loses an entire conversation with no message and no recovery path.

23. **`Instructions.kt:97-98` — glob instruction entries load only the first match.** The in-source comment admits the partial implementation ("For now single-file entries cover the common case; glob entries use the first match"), so `AGENTS.md`-style multi-file instruction directories are silently truncated to one file. `fetchRemote` failures at `:110-112` are likewise silent.

24. **`agent/LlmClient.kt:140` — streamed tool-call names are unconditionally concatenated.** `slot.name = if (slot.name.isEmpty()) it else slot.name + it` corrupts providers that resend the full name per delta (`get_weatherget_weather`), while the non-streaming path at `:180-184` reads the name once. Inconsistent and breaks tool dispatch against real gateways.

25. **`assets/node/boot.js:987-990, 632-633` — the "Node.js" runtime is not Node-compatible.** Rhino cannot run `class`, top-level `await`, `import`, or streams, and `async function` is textually rewritten. The npx tab (`ui/AppViewModel.kt:763` reports `JsRuntime.VERSION`) and `MiniShell` promise real npm semantics, but the majority of modern packages fail to load. The npx surface is advertised more broadly than the runtime supports.

## MINOR

26. **`runtime/Exec.kt:11-13, 35, 53-58` — dead API.** `ScriptRuntime` has no implementation or reference, `RuntimeKind.from` has no callers, and `ExecResult.isSuccess` has no callers. (`OutputListener`'s default no-op methods at `:40-45` are intentional callback defaults, not dead code.)

27. **`agent/AgentSettings.kt:20, 24` — unused constants.** `ZEN_AUTH_URL` and `GITHUB_API` are never referenced; `ui/AgentScreen.kt:802, 824, 828` hardcodes the same `https://opencode.ai/auth` string instead of using the constant, so the two can drift.

28. **`MiniShell.kt:546` — unused parameter.** `runCodeFile(ext: String, ...)` never reads `ext`; callers pass `"py"`/`"js"` (`:404`, `:421`) while the body derives the extension from the `python` flag.

29. **`MiniShell.kt:200, 208` — `env` and `uname` ignore their arguments.** Both return hardcoded constants, so `env -i` or `uname -a` silently produce wrong output instead of an error.

30. **`MiniShell.kt:235` — `ls -l` reports size 0 for directories** (`e.length()` is meaningless for a directory).

31. **`MiniShell.kt:60, 76-95` — only `&&` is supported.** `||`, `;`, and `&` fall through to the unknown-command path, so a failed step is usually followed by a confusing `Unknown command` rather than the standard short-circuit.

32. **`runtime/js/JsRuntime.kt:216` — exceptions from the user `exit` handler are swallowed** (`catch (_: Exception) { }`), hiding cleanup failures.

33. **`ui/AgentScreen.kt:653, 725` — tap handlers are `{}`.** This is deliberate for the copy-on-long-press surface, but the row still renders with clickable affordance while doing nothing on tap, so it reads as a broken control.
